Hakeem Jeffries, leader of the Democrats in the Chamber of Deputies, says he is a «hard yes», in favour without doubts. The Democrats won the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate in the midterm elections, but the new Congress will take office in January. The current Republican majority is slim, so votes from Republicans are needed. Hegseth would be the third cabinet secretary to be impeached, after William Belknap in 1876, who was acquitted by the Senate, and Alejandro Mayorkas in 2024, with charges dismissed.

Officers shot and arrested him, and the man was taken to hospital, where he died, the Polish police said, according to Reuters.

The Polish authorities report six dead, four women and two men, and fifteen injured, including two officers, report Reuters, Al Jazeera and Il Post. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński says one of the two officers is in critical condition. Police chief Marek Boron says a British citizen is among the dead, and two victims have not yet been identified. Initial tolls were lower, with five dead and twelve injured, and Al Jazeera initially spoke of at least three dead.

The man, a 24-year-old Pole, holds a gun licence and has no criminal record, Il Post writes. In witness videos he wore military clothes; Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz denied that he was a soldier. Kierwiński says several weapons were found in the car and that there is no reason to believe there were accomplices. According to the minister, initial investigations indicate an attraction to far-right ideologies, and he describes him as holding «very radical» views. The motive has not been established.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk says three bodies, two women and one man, probably close relatives, were found in the attacker's home. The TV station TVN24, cited by Il Post, speaks of his parents and sister, but the police have not confirmed this.

Tusk called the attack terrorism and the most serious ever to have occurred in Poland, praised the police response, and declared two days of national mourning, ANSA and Al Jazeera report. Mayor Łukasz Gibała declared city mourning until 11 November. President Karol Nawrocki awaits a full explanation. According to Al Jazeera, citing police data, it is the deadliest mass shooting in Poland since 1989, and in 2025 over 50,000 firearm licences were issued, for a total of 411,000.

US President Donald Trump said in a White House briefing on 9 November that no military action is needed in Iran at present, ANSA reports. He had told CNN that new strikes are «very unlikely» if talks advance, and according to Al Jazeera he also said the US blockade of land routes to Iran is in place. He expects to discuss Iran with Xi and Putin at the APEC summit. According to ANSA, oil fell on hopes of progress in the negotiations: at 20:50 Brent dropped 5.6% to $92.8 a barrel and WTI 4.1% to 87.1.

On Tehran, Reuters reports that a senior Iranian official links the talks to the satisfaction of seven demands, including sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while Washington says the nuclear issue must enter negotiations from the start. Qatar, which is mediating, denies that the talks have failed. Rubio said the war is unpopular but «necessary» to stop the nuclear threat, Al Jazeera reports. Reuters could not independently confirm the incidents involving ships reported by the two sides.

On Saturday, US Central Command announced the Iron Gate task force, based in Tampa, against Iranian transfers by land and from the Caspian, Al Jazeera and Reuters report. According to the same Command, the naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion of crude oil. A US aircraft struck the stern of the ship Huda in the Gulf of Oman; since July, the Command says, 147 ships have been diverted and five disabled.

On the attacks, accounts differ. Iranian media report explosions in Qeshm, Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas; the IRNA agency speaks of two missiles falling on Qeshm and semi-official media cite no casualties. Trump described the strikes as «minor», aimed according to the Times of Israel at an anti-aircraft facility. Iranian authorities say the army is stronger than at the beginning of the war, ANSA reports. The Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit mines near Hormuz, and Tehran threatens a very harsh response, Al Jazeera writes.

On the diplomatic front, on 8 November Secretary of State Rubio called some Iranian demands «outrageous and ridiculous», ANSA reports. Trump says Tehran still wants a deal and that he would prefer a diplomatic route. He considers new attacks «very unlikely» if talks advance on the nuclear issue and the reopening of Hormuz. The talks are mediated by Qatar, whose prime minister told Oxford that the US and Iran must not wait for the «perfect moment» for a deal.

According to Bloomberg, cited by the Times of Israel, a draft provides for the reopening of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief, followed by broader nuclear talks. Fox News reports that Trump has discussed new strikes with advisers, and sources cited by the Times of Israel indicate 9 November as the date preferred by the military.

Al Jazeera also writes that a drone caused an explosion and halted production at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq.
